chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Friendship with Freddie Guy and passing road time
summary: He stayed close to nondrinking Freddie Guy, read and napped on the road, and Guy moved from banjo to guitar before leaving for Chicago.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you have any special good friend in the band -- any strong friendship with any particular musician?
I used to pal with the guitar player, Freddie Guy. He and I -- well we didn't socialize. I never drank at all and so we usually stayed close to the person that did the same thing you did.
I didn't even play bridge, which was a reason for staying to myself most of the time. Everybody played bridge. And I couldn't stand it.
You said you used a lot of the travel
time to take a nap -- get some rest I know.
On the bus and such as that, yes. That was -- I couldn't sleep. I can't sleep too well. So every time I get a chance I'd lay down and relax. Otherwise I'd gone crazy.
I think in Unicoe's (PHONETIC) description of who was doing what on one trip, he mentioned Lawrence Brown as reading a book.
I used to read quite a bit. Yes, at first and then I got tired of that.
So what did you do? On the road --

Mostly I would get on the routine and of going to bed and getting up the next day and take in a movie or something like that. And by the time you had dinner and everything, it's time to go back to work. So just exhausted the time that way.
Well how long was Freddie Guy in the band when you knew him.

Oh, I can't -- He was there quite awhile. Because at first -- when I first joined the band -- he was playing banjo. And he finally went into guitar playing. And then after awhile it didn't seem worthwhile to have a rhythm instrument like that.
See guitars hadn't become popular at all. You'd get a guitar anywhere. And they weren't precious. But then
the era hit when -- gee, everything was guitars.
When are you talking about -- at which point?
Later on -- up to now. Even now everything --
How did Freddie Guy leave? Did he leave or was it Duke's idea or --
I think -- no, Duke just sort of -- just figured that it was an excess carriage and he'd rather stay home. He'd rather [him] stay home. So he had a job there in Chicago. And so he went into that.
